page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.16xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the KVM hypervisor within the Enhanced g5ne server family. The system features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 256 GB of memory. Maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation, each core is provisioned with 4.0 GB of RAM, catering to standard enterprise resource architectures.

The hardware configuration includes neither bundled local storage nor discrete GPU accelerators, meaning persistent data operations rely on network-attached block volumes. To handle data transfer demands, the instance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, providing substantial throughput for data-heavy inter-service communication.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the server provides high core density and dedicated CPU execution, removing the impact of resource contention. Decoupling storage allows capacity and IOPS to be provisioned independently without paying for unneeded local disks. The instance is suited for distributed database clusters, enterprise application servers, large-scale continuous integration workers, and containerized backend microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.16xlarge is a general purpose instance running on the KVM hypervisor within the Enhanced server family. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 64 dedicated virtual cores paired with 256 GB of total memory, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates no local NVMe or SSD storage and features no GPU acceleration, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent operational files. Network performance is characterized by a high baseline throughput of 30 Gbps, enabling rapid communication across distributed infrastructure. With its dedicated compute allocation and ample bandwidth profile, this instance is suited for multi-threaded enterprise services, middle-tier application servers, relational databases utilizing cloud disks, and containerized back-end deployments requiring predictable CPU execution.
